workItem.title: Export invoices as CSV
workItem.description:
As a finance clerk
I want to download the invoice list as a CSV file
so that I can reconcile invoices in my spreadsheet at month-end close.

Today Finance copies the invoice table from the UI page by page. That takes about two hours at every month-end close and is error-prone (screenshot from Mira below).
[image]

Scope: backend endpoint only. The export button in the UI is a separate story under Invoice UI refresh.
Use the same filters as the invoice list (GET /api/invoices).
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/invoices/export.csv returns text/csv; charset=utf-8 with Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="invoices-<yyyyMMdd>.csv" (date from the injected TimeProvider).
Supports the same status and customerId filters as the list endpoint, plus optional from/to issue dates (inclusive).
Columns, in order: Number,Customer,IssueDate,DueDate,Currency,Total,Status. Dates yyyy-MM-dd, totals with invariant culture and 2 decimals.
Fields containing a comma, quote or newline are quoted per RFC 4180.
At most 10,000 rows. If more match, respond 422 with a problem-details message.

siblings.title: Invoice total off by 0.01 for some line combinations
Include customer VAT number in export
Export invoice lines as a separate file
Email the export link to Finance
Add export button to invoice list
Add a totals row to the export
Run large exports as a background job

comments.author: Tom Brandt
comments.text: QA plan ready: filters, date range inclusive on both ends, 422 above 10,000 rows, quoting of commas, quotes and newlines. @Dana Novak ping me when the branch is pushed.

comments.author: Ines Duarte
comments.text: Reminder: the export contains customer data. It stays behind the same access rules as the invoice list and is never written to shared folders.

comments.author: Dana Novak
comments.text: Filename will be invoices-yyyyMMdd.csv from the injected TimeProvider, not DateTime.Now (coding standards).

comments.author: Jonas Eklund
comments.text: The export button comes with the UI refresh feature. Nothing needed in src/frontend for this story.

comments.author: Mira Castell
comments.text: Update after talking to Finance again: the semicolon is not needed, plain comma is fine. Their spreadsheet import handles RFC 4180 CSV.

comments.author: Tom Brandt
comments.text: QA note: I will test with customer names containing commas and quotes. The seed data has Eskholt Interiors, Ltd. and Grisdale "Old Mill" Brewing.

comments.author: Mira Castell
comments.text: Cap it at 10,000 rows. Finance always filters by month; if more match, return an error that tells them to narrow the filter.

comments.author: Dana Novak
comments.text: What should happen for very large exports? Production has roughly 180k invoices.

comments.author: Mira Castell
comments.text: One row per invoice. Lines are a separate story if Finance ever needs them.
